jit_decision: No JIT extension: the measured indexed-query hotspot is original-source JSON decoding/validation, not a demonstrated regex control-flow hotspot. Existing regex implementation and VM/JIT equivalence contracts are unchanged.

limitations: Shared macOS host; warm filesystem caches, newly built tables, and fresh predicate membership per request. This is not a cold-storage benchmark.
Linux is native ARM64 ISA in a Docker VM on this same Mac, with a two-CPU quota; it is not independent physical Linux hardware. Linux process CPU samples have scheduler-tick resolution.
Process CPU includes background server work. RSS and macOS physical footprint include ingestion, mappings and allocator retention; 5 ms sampling is not an allocation limit.
First-result latency includes exact-count completion and full JSON response decoding. Source throughput counts verified source bytes, not disk bandwidth.
Within-binary environment controls isolate optional batching/projection, but full-DOM controls retain the new direct scratch parser allocation strategy.

Benchmarks do not establish upstream regex/ripgrep parity, real-provider decision quality, Windows runtime behavior, or zero-cost requests. Named indexes built with the prior prefix-only analyzer require reindexing.
